newsitem.title: HUNGARY: LINAMAR HUNGARY UNIT POISED FOR GROWTH - CSFB.
newsitem.headline: LINAMAR HUNGARY UNIT POISED FOR GROWTH - CSFB.

text.p: Hungary's Mezogep Rt, majority-owned by Canada's Linamar Corp, is seen by CS First Boston (CSFB) as an attractive choice when listed on the Budapest Stock Exchange.

"The Hungarian automotive sector is...on track to be the largest export sector, yet this is the first chance for equity investors to tap into this growth," Spencer Jakab, CSFB's Budapest-based analyst said in a company research.
Mezogep, which produces automotive components and agricultural machinery, is expected to apply for listing on the Budapest Stock Exchange in early March.

The company is 89.6 percent owned by Linamar, with the rest held by board members, CSFB said. It added that assuming an 1,600 forints per share issue price, Linamar's stake would be reduced to 60.3 percent and Mezogep would raise some 4.2 billion forints.
"The timing appears to be optimal as European auto manufacturers are expanding their outsourcing efforts," Jakab said.

Despite a one-off setback due to a strike at one of its main customers, General Motors , last year and temporary cutbacks in agricultural product orders, CSFB expects a steep growth in Mezogep's sales.
"Sales are expected to increase 120 percent in real terms between 1996 and 2001," Jakab said.
Within these, automotive sales with a margin double of agricultural margins, are seen as growing faster by 193 percent over the next five years.
Mezogep's 1996 sales were 4.05 billion forints of which exports accounted for 76 percent, with 44 percent of total sales going to north America and 31 percent to west Europe.

"With inexpensive skilled labour and favourable georgaphic location...the company is highly competitive in the west European market and can utilise the reputation and contacts of Linamar in north America," Jakab said.
The domestic market for automotive components is also expected to grow over the next years by almost 20 percent per year, he said.
Hungarian automotive production includes GM-owned Adam Opel AG, Audi Hungaria and Magyar Suzuki , all of which have plans for future expansion in the country.
